office.scene: Marlowe & Vale Investigations — South Dock District
office.text:
The radiator coughs more than it heats. Rain drags down the office window in crooked lines that make the city look melted.

Mrs. Esther Bell sits across from your desk with gloves still on. Rich fabric. Nervous hands.

'My husband disappeared three nights ago,' she says. 'The police say gambling debt. They're wrong.'

She slides a matchbook across the desk.

THE ORPHEUM CLUB.

choices.label: Ask why she came to you specifically

why_you.text:
'Because my husband trusted you once.'

That lands harder than it should.

She watches your face carefully after she says it, like she's checking whether a ghost moved behind your eyes.

You honestly don't remember Harvey Bell.

overlays.text: Or maybe you do, and the whiskey's just done good work on him.

choices.label: Tell her memory isn't what it used to be

refuse_case.text:
You tell her there's nothing good waiting at the bottom of missing persons cases anymore.

She nods like she expected that answer before she walked in.

On her way out, she pauses by the frosted glass door.

'If someone asks whether you saw me,' she says quietly, 'you didn't.'

choices.label: Stop her and take the case anyway

window_watch.text:
From the window you watch a black sedan parked across the street.

Two men inside. Hats low. One lights a cigarette but neither of them smoke it.

They're watching your office.

When Mrs. Bell exits the building, the sedan pulls away without following her.

overlays.text: That means they already know where she's going.

choices.label: Lock the office and forget the whole thing

insets.text: MATCHBOOK  —  THE ORPHEUM CLUB  —  No windows. No clocks.

take_case.text:
The Orpheum smells like wet wool, expensive perfume, and the kind of money that survives recessions.

A piano murmurs somewhere behind the smoke.

The bartender glances at the matchbook in your hand and loses a little color.

watch_room.text:
Three card tables. Two city councilmen. A union fixer pretending not to recognize you.

Near the back wall sits a thin man reading a newspaper upside down.

Nobody else seems to notice him.

overlays.text: You saw him once before. Maybe outside a courthouse. Maybe at a funeral.

bartender.text:
The bartender dries the same glass the entire time you talk.

'Bell came in Tuesday,' he says. 'Met somebody upstairs. Left nervous.'

'Who'd he meet?'

The bartender looks toward the ceiling.

'Nobody I saw.'

bartender_paid.text:
Your last five-dollar bill disappears under the glass.

The bartender finally looks at you directly.

'Room 204 upstairs. But if anybody asks, you were never here.'

bartender_pressure.text:
You push too hard.

The piano stops.

Not dramatically. Just all at once, like somebody remembered a cue.

The bartender steps back from you.

'You should leave,' he says softly.

thin_man.text:
Up close, the thin man smells faintly medicinal.

Without lowering the newspaper, he says:

'If you're looking for Bell, stop before you become part of the paperwork.'

choices.label: Pretend you don't know what he's talking about

paperwork.text:
'Men disappear,' he says. 'Then records change. Debts appear. Signatures move around. Whole lives become bookkeeping errors.'

He folds the newspaper.

The obituary page.

Every name circled in pencil.

overlays.text: Second time through, you notice one circled name: Harvey Bell.

choices.label: Go upstairs before he disappears too

street_again.text:
The rain feels colder after the club.

Across the street, the same black sedan from earlier idles beneath a dead streetlamp.

choices.label: Circle back into the club through the alley

insets.text: Second Floor  —  Carpets thick enough to hide footsteps

back_hall.text:
The upstairs hallway is too quiet for a place this crowded.

At the far end: Room 204.

Halfway there, you notice a janitor's cart beside a service door.

janitor_cart.text:
Under the rags and bleach bottles sits a stack of burned paper scraps.

One piece still readable:

BELL, HARVEY — ACCOUNT CLOSED.

insets.text: The scrap in your pocket matches the stationery on the desk. Same letterhead. Same hand.

room_204.text:
The room is empty except for cigarette smoke that hasn't had time to fade.

A coat hangs over the chair.

Harvey Bell's wallet sits open on the desk beside a ledger filled with names, dates, and payment amounts.

choices.label: Leave before whoever was here comes back

coat.text:
Inside the coat pocket is a photograph.

You and Harvey Bell outside a courthouse, both younger by ten years.

On the back, in your handwriting:

IF ANYTHING HAPPENS, DON'T TRUST CITY HALL.

overlays.text: You really didn't remember him. That's the worst part.

insets.text: BELL, H.  —  DELIVERED LEDGER  —  ACCOUNT CLOSED
You've gathered enough to piece it together. The ledger is the last link.

ledger.text:
The ledger isn't gambling debt.

It's payoffs.

Judges. Dock officials. Police captains.

Every payment marked with the same symbol in the margin: a small black circle.

choices.label: Take the ledger to the police
Sell the ledger back to the people named inside

hall_return.text:
You turn back toward the stairs.

Two men are already climbing them.

Black coats. Calm faces.

The same men from the sedan.

choices.label: Try to bluff your way past

records_room.text:
The service stairs lead below the club into a records room bigger than the club itself.

Shelves of city files disappear into darkness.

Birth certificates. Arrest reports. Tax records.

Lives stacked like inventory.

overlays.text: This wasn't about Harvey Bell. Harvey Bell just noticed it.
You wrote that warning on the photograph years ago. You already knew.

harvey_file.text:
Harvey Bell's file is thin.

Too thin.

Inside is only a death certificate dated tomorrow morning.{pause}

Tomorrow morning.

deep_shelves.text:
You keep searching.

More files with future dates.

Future arrests.

Future deaths.

At the end of the aisle you finally find {player_name} typed neatly on a folder tab.

overlays.text: Maybe the city isn't corrupt. Maybe it's rehearsed.
The thin man. The newspaper. The circled names. It's the same system, running itself.

choices.label: Walk away while you still can

police_end.text:
The desk sergeant goes pale when he sees the ledger.

You spend six hours giving statements.

By morning, the ledger has disappeared from evidence.

So has the sergeant.

overlays.text: A clerk quietly tells you to stop asking questions if you want to stay alive.

sell_end.text:
They pay you enough money to retire twice.

Nobody threatens you.

Nobody raises their voice.

One man simply says:

'Mr. Bell made the mistake of believing information should belong to the public.'

overlays.text: Cashier's Check  —  Valid at any national bank

caught_end.text:
'Evening, {player_name},' one of the men says.

The other takes your gun before you think to reach for it.

They're polite about the whole thing.

That somehow makes it worse.

burn_end.text:
The files burn faster than paper should.

Within minutes the room is choking black smoke through the vents above the club.

You leave through the alley while sirens begin somewhere far away.

By morning, half the city's records are gone.

For a few weeks afterward, people disappear less often.

truth_end.text:
You meet Esther Bell before sunrise and hand her the certificate.

She reads it once.

Doesn't cry.

'He thought if he could prove it existed, somebody honest would stop it,' she says.

Across the river, City Hall glows through the fog.

overlays.text: Harvey Bell  —  Official Time of Death: 8:14 AM tomorrow
You don't tell her your name was in there too.

conspiracy_end.text:
Inside your file is a photograph taken through your office window.

Tonight.

On the back:

SUBJECT HAS REOPENED INQUIRY.

Below that:

ACCOUNT PENDING CLOSURE.

overlays.text: You suddenly understand why the thin man smelled like hospital antiseptic.
And why Harvey Bell looked nervous in every memory you still have left of him.

coward_end.text:
You lock the office, pour two fingers of cheap bourbon, and tell yourself you made the smart choice.

Three days later, somebody slips an obituary under your door.{pause}

Harvey Bell.

You don't remember the man.

But you recognize your own handwriting on the envelope.

sedan.text:
The sedan pulls away before you reach it.

As it passes, the passenger tosses something onto the sidewalk.

A photograph.

You, asleep at your desk.

overlays.text: {noticed_tail?The same angle as whoever was watching from across the street. They've had eyes on you since before she walked in.|Somebody has been watching you long enough to know your habits.}
